title.narrative: Integrated Food Production Response to Famine-Affected Community in Sirba Locality of West Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtThe conflict in Sudan has led to the displacement of over 10.4 million people, including 8 million internally displaced persons (IDPs) and 2.2 million refugees in neighboring countries. The latest IPC analysis indicates that 24.6 million people in Sudan face acute food insecurity, with 756,340 people in IPC Phase 3+ in West Darfur. The crisis disproportionately affects women and girls, exacerbating existing gender disparities and limiting their access to food, health, nutrition, and essential services. This has increased protection risks, including mental health challenges and gender-based violence (GBV). Communities resort to negative coping mechanisms, such as diverting funds from essential services to prioritize food, which further deepens vulnerabilities. Women, girls, and children face heightened risks of rape, intimate partner violence (IPV), and child marriage as consequences of food insecurity.ltbrgtThis project aims to address key drivers of humanitarian needs and reduce the risk of famine in Sirba (IPC 4). It will promote food production through food security and livelihood (FSL) interventions, supporting 600 household farmers with improved seedlings and agricultural extension training. Additionally, essential livestock protection services, including vaccination and treatment, will target 5,250 pastoral and agro-pastoral households. These activities will benefit 1,500 households, treating 37,500 animals and vaccinating 150,000 animals, thereby enhancing food security and enabling households to generate income from harvests and dairy products after meeting their food needs. This will reduce the diversion of household funds from essential services.ltbrgtThe integration of nutrition, health, and protection services will improve household livelihoods by addressing malnutrition and providing lifesaving support. Nutrition services will include treatment for severe acute malnutrition (SAM) with medical complications at stabilization centers (SCs), benefiting 281 cases, and outpatient therapeutic programs (OTPs) for 1,876 under-five SAM cases. Moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) in under-fives and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) will be addressed through targeted supplementary feeding programs (TSFPs). Community-based interventions, supported by 10 community nutrition volunteers (CNVs) and 10 community health promoters (CHPs), will align with Health and Nutrition Cluster guidelines to effectively meet the needs of famine-affected populations.ltbrgtHealth services will reach 113,190 individuals with integrated primary healthcare (PHC), including maternal and child health services, immunizations, mental health consultations, and essential drugs. Survivors of GBV will receive timely, comprehensive support through a One-Stop Center (OSC) at Sirba Hospital, offering case management, psychosocial support, counseling, and sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services. The OSC will be equipped with 20 PEP kits, and health workers will be trained in clinical management of rape (CMR). GBV survivors requiring higher-level care will receive cash or in-kind assistance.ltbrgtCommunity-based GBV prevention will include a women’s center, six protection networks, and training for 50 service providers to enhance GBV awareness, prevention, and active referral pathways to the OSC.ltbrgtThe consortium partners (WR, VSF-G, HOPE, and HPDO) will work collaboratively to navigate contextual challenges, engage local authorities and community leaders, and adopt a conflict-sensitive approach. These efforts aim to reduce ethnic tensions and promote reconciliation between farmers and herders through protection networks and general protection activities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
